Taking a thousand births as one transformation,
Taking myriad differences as one origin.
Possessing essence but not using it,
Possessing spirit but not employing it,
Preserving the simplicity of the great undifferentiated,
Establishing oneself in the center of utmost refinement,
When sleeping, one does not dream,
One's wisdom does not sprout,
One's movement has no form,
One's stillness has no substance,
Existing as if absent,
Living as if dead,
Entering and exiting without gaps,
Employing ghosts and spirits.
This is how the spirit can ascend to the Dao.
Making the spirit flow freely without losing its origin,
Day and night without interruption, being at one with things like springtime,
This is uniting and giving birth to the opportune time in the heart.
Therefore, the body may decay, but the spirit never transforms.
To respond to change with the unchanging,
through thousands of transformations and myriad revolutions, yet without ever reaching an end.
That which changes reverts to the formless,
while that which does not change is born together with Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, that which gives life has never been born,
that which is born is what is born.
That which transforms has never transformed,
that which is transformed is what is transformed.
This is the wandering of the True Person (Zhēn rén),
the pure and unadulterated Dao.
*Fú Yán*
Lǎo Zǐ said:
The Dao is supremely high without anything above it,
supremely deep without anything below it.
It is as level as a plumb line,
as straight as a string,
as round as a compass,
as square as a carpenter's square,
encompassing Heaven and Earth without inside or outside,
penetrating and universally covering without any obstruction.
Therefore, those who embody the Dao,
are neither angry nor happy.
When they sit, they have no worries;
when they sleep, they do not dream.
They see things and name them;
when affairs arrive, they respond.
Lǎozǐ said:
Those who desire to seize fame through corpses [i.e., exploit misfortune for personal gain] must pretend to do good;
those who pretend to do good will inevitably create problems.
Once problems arise, they abandon the public good and pursue personal interests,
turn their back on the proper way and rely on their own judgment.
If they desire to be praised and thus do good,
establish a reputation and thus become esteemed,
then their governance will not accord with principle, and their actions will not accord with the times.
If governance does not accord with principle, there will be many reproaches;
if actions do not accord with the times, there will be no success.
Acting rashly to seek the right outcome,
even if successful, it is not enough to offset the blame;
if things fail, it is enough to destroy oneself.
Lǎozǐ said:
Do not act to seize fame,
do not be a storehouse of schemes,
do not take on responsibility for affairs,
do not be a master of wisdom.
Conceal yourself in the formless,
act without delay in the unseen,
do not be the first to seek blessings,
do not be the originator of misfortune.
Begin in the formless,
act only when compelled.
If you desire blessings before misfortune,
you must desire profit before avoiding harm.
Therefore, those who are at peace through *wúwéi* 无为 [non-action],
To lose the means of securing tranquility is to invite danger.
He who governs through inaction,
if he loses the means of governing, will bring chaos.
Therefore,
"Do not desire to be commonplace like jade,
but rather unique like stone."
He whose patterns are beautiful will surely have his skin peeled.
He whose horns are beautiful will surely have his body slaughtered.
A sweet spring will surely be exhausted.
A straight tree will surely be felled.
Flowery and glorious words will later become transgressions.
If stone contains jade,
it injures the mountain.
The woes of the common people (qiánshǒu),
are indeed prior to words.
Lǎozǐ said:
The course of time,
acts in accordance with it;
he who does not understand the Dao, fortune becomes misfortune.
The sky is the cover,
the earth is the base,
he who is good at using the Dao will never be exhausted.
The earth is the base,
the sky is the cover,
he who is good at using the Dao will never be harmed.
If you array the five elements, there must be a victor.
All that is covered by Heaven is without exception assessed.
Therefore,
"To know when you know,
is a sickness."
Lǎozǐ said:
is best; to not know when you know,
Mountains produce metal,
stones produce jade,
yet they turn against each other and are stripped away;
wood breeds insects,
which in turn devour it;
people create affairs,
which in turn harm them.
Those who love activity are never without hitting the mark (meeting trouble),
those who strive for profit are never without being exhausted;
the skilled swimmer drowns,
the skilled rider falls;
each with what they love,
instead make disaster for themselves.
Success lies in timing,
not in striving;
governance lies in the Way (Dào),
not in sages.
Earth dwells low,
not striving for height,
therefore it is secure and not in danger;
water flows downward,
not striving for speed,
Therefore, leaving without delay.
"Therefore, the sage has no attachments, so he has nothing to lose;
he takes no action, so he suffers no defeat."
Lǎozǐ said:
One statement cannot be exhausted;
two statements are the foundation of the world;
three statements make the feudal lords powerful;
four statements make the world unparalleled.
If one is steadfast and trustworthy, then he cannot be exhausted;
if one possesses morality, then he is the foundation of the world;
promoting the virtuous,
makes the feudal lords powerful;
hating the few and loving the many makes the world unparalleled.
Lǎozǐ said:
People have three ways to die
not destined by fate:
eating and drinking without moderation,
treating one's body lightly,
sicknesses will jointly kill them;
taking pleasure without limit,
being greedy without stopping,
punishments will jointly kill them;
using a few to offend the many,
using weakness to bully the strong,
weapons will jointly kill them.
Lǎozǐ said:
Those who give generously will receive a handsome reward.
Those whose resentment is great will suffer a deep calamity.
To give sparingly and hope for much in return,
to harbor resentment and expect no trouble,
such a thing has never been.
Examine the way someone goes,
and you will know the way they will return.
Lǎozǐ said:
Investigate Tiānmìng (the Mandate of Heaven),
govern the methods of the mind,
regulate likes and dislikes,
accord with one's natural disposition;
then the way of governance will be clear.
To investigate Tiānmìng is to be free from confusion about misfortune and fortune.
To govern the methods of the mind is to be free from unjustified joy and anger.
To regulate likes and dislikes is to not covet what is useless.
To accord with one's natural disposition is to keep desires within proper bounds.
Being free from confusion about misfortune and fortune means that movement and stillness accord with principle.
Being free from unjustified joy and anger means that rewards and punishments are impartial.
Not coveting what is useless means not harming one's nature with desires.
Keeping desires within proper bounds means nourishing life with contentment.
All these four things
are not sought from the outside,
are not borrowed from others;
they are obtained by looking within oneself.
Lǎozǐ said:
Do not seek actions that can be criticized,
do not hate others for criticizing yourself,
cultivate virtues sufficient for praise,
do not seek others to praise yourself.
If you cannot prevent misfortune from arriving,
believe that you did not invite it;
if you cannot make fortune certainly come,
believe that you did not reject it.
The arrival of misfortune is not of one's own making,
therefore, one is not worried when poor.
The coming of fortune is not of one's own accomplishment,
therefore, one is not arrogant when successful.
Therefore, one lives in leisure and is happy,
governs through non-action.
Lǎozǐ said:
The Dao is to preserve what one already has,
not to seek what one has not yet obtained.
Seeking what one has not yet obtained means that what one already has will be lost.
Following what one already has means that what one desires will arrive.
Governance is not strengthened by preventing disorder,
and those who govern through action will certainly be in danger.
Actions are not exempt from having faults,
and those who eagerly seek fame will certainly be thwarted.
Therefore, no blessing is greater than being without misfortune,
and no benefit is greater than not losing.
"Therefore, things are sometimes diminished by increasing them,
"To diminish it is to increase it."
Now, the Dao cannot be urged upon those who seek profit,
but it can bring peace of mind and avoidance of harm.
Therefore, it is always without misfortune, but not always with blessings;
it is always without fault, but not always with merit.
The Dao is described as vast and obscure,
following the majesty of Heaven,
sharing the same breath as Heaven.
It has no thought,
no planned provisions.
It does not welcome those who come,
nor does it see off those who leave.
Though people go east, west, south, and north,
it stands alone in the center.
Therefore, dwelling amidst the crookedness of the multitude,
it does not lose its straightness;
flowing along with the world,
it does not depart from its domain.
It does not strive for good,
nor does it avoid ugliness;
it follows the Dao of Heaven.
It does not seek to be first,
nor does it insist on its own way;
it follows the principles of Heaven.
It does not plan in advance,
nor does it abandon the present;
it makes its appointment with Heaven.
It does not seek gain,
Not declining fortune
follows the laws of Heaven.
Internally there are no unusual blessings,
externally there are no unusual disasters.
Therefore, disasters and blessings do not arise,
and how could there be human thieves?
Therefore, in the highest virtue, words share the same general idea,
and actions share the same direction.
Those above and below are of one mind,
and there are no divergent paths to be seen.
That which is deviant is sent away in decline,
and the path to goodness is opened,
and the people head in the right direction.
Lǎozǐ said:
When someone does good, give encouragement;
when someone does not do good, observe them.
Encouragement leads to the birth of nobility,
observation leads to the birth of troubles.
Therefore, the Dào cannot be advanced to seek fame,
but can be retreated to cultivate oneself.
Therefore, the sage does not seek fame through actions,
nor seek praise through knowledge.
Governance follows nature,
and the self has nothing to do with it.
Those who act may not succeed,
those who seek may not obtain.
People may be limited, but the Dào has no limit in reaching everywhere.
Having wisdom but not acting is the same as having no wisdom;
having ability but having nothing to do is the same as having no virtue.
Having wisdom as if having no wisdom,
having ability as if having no ability,
When principles are fully understood, then talent is extinguished.
People and the Dao cannot both be manifest.
If people love fame, then they do not use the Dao.
If the Dao prevails over people, then fame ceases.
If the Dao ceases and fame is prominent, then there is danger and ruin.
Lǎozǐ said:
"To have trustworthy people distribute wealth
is not as good as determining shares and drawing lots."
Why is this?
Because the fairness of those who have intentions
is not as good as those who are without intentions.
"To have honest people guard wealth
is not as good as closing the door and sealing it completely,"
because the integrity of those who have desires
is not as good as those who are without desires.
People resent it when their flaws are pointed out;
a mirror that shows ugliness is a good mirror.
If a person can deal with things and not involve oneself,
then one will be free from burdens.
Lǎozǐ said:
"Generally, those who employ people
do not value their precious gifts,
Must use humble language.
If the gifts are meager but desires are insatiable,
and one acts humbly but avoids expressing regrets,
debating but failing to establish connections,
making covenants and oaths,
and setting dates but repeatedly failing to meet them,
therefore, the 君子 (jūnzǐ) does not outwardly adorn himself with benevolence and righteousness,
but inwardly cultivates morality and virtue.
He cultivates the affairs within his territory,
maximizes the extent of his land,
encourages the people to defend to the death,
strengthens his city walls,
and unites those above and below in one heart,
to defend the altars of the soil and grain together.
One who seeks fame does not boast of blamelessness,
and one who seeks profit does not attack what is difficult to obtain.
This is the way to certain preservation,
the principle of certain benefit.
老子 (Lǎozǐ) said:
The sage overcomes his heart (mind),
the masses overcome their desires,
the 君子 (jūnzǐ) walks the path of 正氣 (zhèngqì, upright qi),
the petty person walks the path of 衺氣 (xiéqì, perverse qi).
That which is internally suitable to one's nature,
and externally aligns with righteousness,
acting in accordance with principle,
and not being bound by things,
This is upright qi;
indulging in flavors,
being excessive in sounds and sights,
erupting in joy and anger,
and not considering future troubles
is depraved qi.
Depraved and upright harm each other,
desires and nature injure each other,
they cannot coexist,
one rises, the other declines,
therefore the sage diminishes desires to follow nature.
The eyes love color,
the ears love sound,
the nose loves fragrance,
the mouth loves taste,
combined to delight in these things,
and inseparable from benefits and harms,
these are desires;
the ears, eyes, nose, and mouth do not know what to take or reject,
all are controlled by the mind,
each attaining its proper place.
From this perspective,
the fact that desires cannot be overcome is also clear.
Lǎozǐ said:
Those who govern the body and nourish the nature
regulate sleeping and dwelling,
moderate eating and drinking,
To harmonize joy and anger,
and to be adaptable in movement and stillness,
those who obtain what is within themselves
will not allow depraved influences to enter.
To adorn the exterior harms the interior,
to indulge the emotions harms the spirit,
and to focus on the appearance obscures the truth.
If one forgets even for a moment that they are striving to be virtuous,
they will inevitably exhaust their nature.
If one never forgets to maintain proper deportment even within a hundred paces,
they will inevitably burden their form.
Therefore, beautiful wings injure the bones,
and luxuriant branches and leaves harm the roots.
Those who can achieve both perfections are non-existent in the world.
Lǎozǐ said:
Heaven, possessing brightness, does not worry about the people's darkness;
Earth, possessing wealth, does not worry about the people's poverty.
Those who attain the Dao are like hills and mountains,
solid and unmoving.
Those who travel use them as landmarks.
They straighten themselves and thus enrich all things;
they do not rely on gifts from others.
Those who employ them do not receive their favor,
therefore they are secure and can endure.
Heaven and Earth give to all
and therefore take nothing away.
They have no virtue
Therefore, there is no resentment.
Those prone to anger are sure to have many grievances;
those skilled at giving are sure to be skilled at taking away.
Only by following the natural way of Heaven and Earth can one overcome principle.
Thus, as soon as praise is seen, destruction follows;
as soon as goodness is seen, evil accompanies it;
benefit is the beginning of harm;
fortune precedes misfortune;
if one does not seek benefit, then there is no misfortune.
The body in its wholeness is the norm;
wealth and nobility are but temporary lodgings.
Lǎozǐ said:
The sage does not have clothes of odd cut,
nor strange and unusual behavior.
His clothing is not mixed or ostentatious;
his behavior is not for show.
He is understanding but not extravagant;
impoverished but not fearful;
honored but not ostentatious;
hidden but not disgraced;
different but not bizarre.
Using the same without being able to name it,
this is called great understanding.
Lǎozǐ said:
The follower of the Dào rectifies himself and waits for destiny.
When the time arrives, it cannot be welcomed and returned;
Time, once gone, cannot be pursued or pulled back.
Therefore, the sages neither advance to seek it,
nor retreat to yield it.
If one follows time for three years,
when time departs, I move on.
If I abandon the moment for three years,
time will lag behind me.
Neither abandoning nor seeking,
stand upright in the center.
The Way of Heaven is impartial;
it only favors virtue.
The arrival of good fortune is not something one seeks for oneself,
therefore one does not boast of one's merit.
The arrival of misfortune is not something one generates oneself,
therefore one does not regret one's actions.
If the center is calm,
one is not burdened by virtue.
One is not startled by the barking of a dog,
and one has confidence in one's true nature.
Being sincere without presumptuous expectations,
therefore, those who are versed in the Dao are not perplexed,
and those who understand destiny are not worried.
When emperors and kings die,
their remains are buried in the wilderness.
When sacrifices are made, they are offered in the Míngtáng (明堂),
for the spirit is valued over the form.
Therefore, when the spirit controls the form, it will obey.
When the form overcomes the spirit, it will be exhausted.
Though intelligence is employed,
it must invariably revert to the divine,
which is called great comprehension.
Lǎozǐ said:
The ancients who preserved themselves,
rejoiced in virtue and forgot lowliness,
therefore fame did not move their will;
rejoiced in the Dao and forgot poverty,
therefore profit did not move their heart.
Therefore, being humble, they could rejoice,
being still, they could be content.
To calculate one's lifespan with numbers,
and worry about the disorder of the world,
is like worrying about the drying up of the river water,
and weeping to add to it.
Therefore, not worrying about the disorder of the world,
but rejoicing that their own person is well-governed,
such a person can be spoken to about the Dao.
Lǎozǐ said:
People have three resentments:
those with high rank are envied by others,
those with high office are disliked by their superiors,
those with abundant salary are resented by others.
The higher the rank, the lower one's intention;
the greater the office, the smaller one's heart;
the more abundant the salary, the more extensive one's giving.
Cultivating these three prevents resentment from arising;
"Therefore, nobility takes lowliness as its root,
Highness takes lowliness as its foundation."
Lǎozǐ said:
Speech is the means by which one communicates oneself to others,
Hearing is the means by which one receives others into oneself,
Being both blind and deaf,
One is cut off from the way of humanity.
Therefore, those who suffer from the affliction of blindness and deafness,
Know nothing of how things connect;
How is it only the physical form that can suffer blindness and deafness!
The mind can have it as well.
When the mind is blocked,
It knows nothing of connection,
This is akin to blindness and deafness.
As for the Dao being the ancestor,
All that has form arises from it,
Its affection is truly close;
All who partake of grains and feed on Qi find longevity,
Its benevolence is truly great;
All wise people learn from it,
Its teaching is truly clear.
People all use the useless to harm the useful,
Therefore, knowledge is not broad and days are insufficient,
Spending the days in games, asking about the Dao,
Hearing and seeing is deep,
Not hearing and not asking,
It is like the blind and deaf compared to other people.
Lǎozǐ said:
In human nature, the heart submits to virtue,
not to force.
Virtue lies in giving,
not in seeking.
Therefore, the sage who desires to be esteemed by others
first esteems others;
who desires to be honored by others
first honors others;
who desires to overcome others
first overcomes himself;
who desires to demean others
first demeans himself.
Therefore, status (high or low), rank (noble or humble),
are regulated by Dào.
The ancient sage-kings, by placing themselves beneath others in speech
and behind others in action,
caused the world to joyfully support them without weariness
and to bear them without burden.
This is because their virtue was abundant and their temperament harmonious.
Therefore, knowing that giving is taking
and placing oneself behind is going before,
is approaching the Dào.
Lǎozǐ said:
One whose virtue is little but whose favor is great will be criticized;
Those who have just descended (in rank or ability) but occupy a high position are in danger;
those who have not performed great deeds but receive generous salaries will decline.
Therefore,
"Things are sometimes increased only to be diminished,
or diminished only to be increased."
Everyone knows the benefit of seeking benefit,
but does not know the harm of seeking benefit.
Only the Sage knows that harm can become benefit,
and benefit can become harm.
Therefore, a tree that bears fruit too often will surely damage its roots;
a family that hoards too much wealth will surely bring disaster upon its descendants.
Indeed, great benefit can turn into harm;
this is the way of Heaven.
Lǎozǐ said:
Petty people act with the thought of "if I can get it" (gǒu dé);
Gentlemen act with the thought of "if it is righteous" (gǒu yì).
One who does good
is not one who seeks fame,
but fame follows them;
fame does not aim to gain profit,
but profit comes to them.
What they seek is the same,
what they aim for is different;
therefore, with every beneficial action,
loss follows.
One whose words are not consistently right,
and whose actions are not consistently appropriate,
A petty person is one who
is perceptive about one matter
and proficient in one skill;
a mediocre person is one who
encompasses and possesses both;
a sage is one who has skills and talents that he employs.
Lǎozǐ said:
Life is what is borrowed,
death is where one returns.
Therefore, when the world is well-governed, one uses righteousness to protect oneself;
when the world is in chaos, one uses oneself to protect righteousness.
The day of death
is the end of one's journey.
Therefore, the *jūnzǐ* (gentleman) is cautious in using it just once.
Therefore, life is what is received from Heaven,
fate is what is encountered in time.
To have talent but not meet the right era
is Heaven's will.
Seeking it has its way,
obtaining it lies in fate.
Therefore, the *jūnzǐ* can do good but cannot be certain of receiving blessings;
he cannot bear to do wrong,
but cannot be certain of avoiding disaster.
Therefore, the *jūnzǐ* advances when the time is right,
obtaining it through righteousness.
What good fortune is there in that?
To retire when the time is not right,
and to yield with propriety,
what misfortune could there be!
Therefore, those who, though in poverty and lowliness, still do not regret it,
have obtained what they value.
Lǎozǐ said:
People have compliant and resistant qi arising in their hearts.
When the heart is well-governed, then the qi is compliant.
When the heart is disordered, then the qi is resistant.
The governance or disorder of the heart lies in the Dao.
To attain the Dao is to govern the heart.
To lose the Dao is to disorder the heart.
When the heart is governed, there is yielding.
When the heart is disordered, there is contention.
Yielding leads to virtue.
Contention leads to the generation of wickedness.
When there is virtue, the qi is compliant.
When wickedness arises, the qi is resistant.
When the qi is compliant, one diminishes oneself to serve others.
When the qi is resistant, one diminishes others to serve oneself.
Qi can be governed and controlled by the Dao.
The Dao of Heaven,
is like the echo responding to sound.
When virtue accumulates, blessings arrive.
When calamity accumulates, resentment arrives.
Learning is ruined by official prosperity.
Filial piety declines with wife and children.
Trouble arises from worry about its resolution;
illness worsens from premature hope of recovery.
Therefore,
"If one is as careful at the end as at the beginning,
then there will be no failures."
Lǎozǐ said:
Accommodating the crooked and the straight,
how can one not succeed?
Accommodating the straight and the crooked,
do not let it go too far.
This is what is meant by "being in the same mud but being different mud."
Lǎozǐ said:
The sage is the same in life and death;
the fool is also the same in life and death.
The sage's sameness in life and death is clear in understanding principles.
The fool's sameness in life and death is not knowing where benefit and harm lie.
The Way (dào) hangs in the sky,
things are spread on the earth,
harmony lies in people.
If the ruler of the people is not in harmony, then the weather from the sky will not descend,
the earth's qi will not rise,
yin and yang will be out of tune,
wind and rain will be untimely,
and the people will suffer from sickness and hunger.
Lǎozǐ said:
To obtain an army of ten thousand,
is not as good as hearing one appropriate word.
To obtain the pearl of Suí Hóu,
is not as good as understanding the reason for things.
To obtain the jade of Hé Shì,
is not as good as understanding the appropriateness of things.
Though the world is large,
those who delight in using armies perish.
Though a country is peaceful,
those who delight in war are endangered.
Therefore,
"A small country with few people,
even if it possesses equipment of tens and hundreds, should not use them."
Lǎozǐ said:
One who can become a Hegemon King,
must be one whose virtue prevails.
One who can defeat an enemy,
must be strong.
One who can be strong,
must be one who utilizes the strength of others.
One who can utilize the strength of others,
must be one who gains the hearts of the people.
One who can gain the hearts of the people,
must be one who understands himself.
One who can understand himself,
must be gentle and weak.
Overpowering those inferior to oneself,
As for resisting those who are like oneself,
and overcoming those who are superior to oneself through gentleness,
their power cannot be measured.
Therefore, being able to turn a certain defeat into a great victory,
only the sage can achieve this.
Dào Dé
Wén Zǐ asked about the Dao.
Lǎozǐ said:
"If learning is not refined,
and listening to the Dao is not profound,
all those who listen
intend to attain wisdom,
intend to perfect their conduct,
and intend to achieve fame and success.
Without refinement, there is no clarity;
without depth, there is no understanding.
Therefore, the highest learning is through spiritual listening,
the middle learning is through mental listening,
and the lowest learning is through ear listening.
Those who listen with their ears
learn only skin-deep.
Those who listen with their mind
learn only in their muscles.
Those who listen with their spirit
learn in their very bones.
Therefore, if listening is not profound,
then knowledge is not clear.
If one's understanding is not clear,
then one cannot exhaust its essence.
If one cannot exhaust its essence,
then one cannot execute it successfully.
In general, to listen to reason,
one must have a receptive and tranquil mind,
reducing one's breath and not being excessive,
without thought or worry,
with eyes that do not look frivolously,
and ears that do not listen carelessly.
Focus the spirit and accumulate,
so that the inner intent is full and complete.
Once you have obtained it,
you must firmly hold onto it;
you must maintain it for a long time.
Now, the Dao,
originates and has a beginning,
beginning in softness and weakness,
and developing into firmness and strength.
It begins in brevity and fewness,
and develops into multitude and length.
A tree that is ten spans around
begins from a handful,
a platform that is a hundred *rèn* high
begins from the ground.
This is the Dao of Heaven.
The sage models after it:
Humility is the way to place oneself below,
To retreat is the means by which to place oneself behind;
frugality is the means by which to make oneself small;
to diminish is the means by which to lessen oneself;
by being humble, one becomes honored;
by retreating, one goes first;
by being frugal, one becomes expansive;
by diminishing, one becomes great.
This is how the Way of Heaven is achieved.
Now, the Dào
is the origin of Virtue (Dé),
the root of Heaven,
the gateway to fortune.
All things depend on it to be born,
depend on it to be completed,
depend on it to find peace.
Now, the Dào
is non-action and formless.
Inwardly, it cultivates the self;
outwardly, it governs people.
When achievements are accomplished and affairs are established,
one dwells as a neighbor to Heaven.
It acts without acting, yet there is nothing that it does not do.
None know its affections,
none know its truth.
Within it, there is trustworthiness.
When the Son of Heaven (Tiānzǐ) possesses the Dào, then all under Heaven submit;
he endures with his altars of soil and grain.
When dukes and marquises possess the Dào, then the people are harmonious and amicable;
One will not lose his state.
If the scholar-commoners possess the Dao, then they will preserve their lives,
and protect their kin.
The powerful become powerful through the Dao,
conquering without battle.
The small and weak gain through the Dao,
obtaining without strife.
Undertaking affairs through the Dao,
one achieves success and gains blessings.
If ruler and ministers possess the Dao, then they are loyal and benevolent.
If father and son possess the Dao, then they are loving and filial.
If scholar-commoners possess the Dao, then they love each other.
Therefore, with the Dao, there is harmony;
without the Dao, there is harshness.
From this perspective,
the Dao, in relation to people,
is universally appropriate.
Now, the Dao,
if practiced to a small extent, brings small blessings;
if practiced to a large extent, brings large blessings;
if practiced to its fullest extent, brings the submission of all under Heaven.
Those who submit cherish it.
Therefore, the Di (帝)
is what all under Heaven goes to.
The Wang (王)
is what all under Heaven heads toward.
If all under Heaven does not go to or head toward them,
They cannot be called emperors or kings.
Therefore, emperors and kings cannot succeed without the right people;
even with the right people, they cannot maintain their rule if they lose the Way (Dào).
Those who lose the Way (Dào) are
extravagant, indulgent, arrogant, and dissipated;
they are negligent, haughty, conceited, and proud;
they see themselves as self-evident and self-illuminating;
they are stubbornly powerful;
they create difficulties and foster resentment;
they become masters of war;
they become leaders of rebellion.
If petty men practice these things,
their bodies will suffer great calamity;
if great men practice these things,
their states will be destroyed,
lightly affecting their own persons,
deeply affecting their descendants.
Therefore, no crime is greater than being without the Way (Wúdào),
and no resentment is deeper than being without virtue (Wúdé);
this is the way of Heaven (Tiāndào).
Lǎozǐ said:
"Those who practice the Way (Dào)
cause people, even if they are brave,
not to be able to pierce them;
even if they are skillful,
not to be able to strike them.
If one cannot be pierced,
To strike and miss,
and still feel humiliated,
is not as good as making even the brave not dare to assassinate,
and even the skilled not dare to strike.
That those who "dare not"
do not lack the intention
is not as good as making people lack the intention.
That those who lack the intention
do not have a heart of love and benefit.
It is not as good as making all the men and women under Heaven
joyfully desire to love and benefit him.
If it is like this,
he is a ruler without territory,
he is a leader without office,
and all under Heaven wish to secure his benefit.
Wén Zǐ asked about virtue.
Lǎo Zǐ said:
"Nourishing them, raising them,
developing them, growing them,
benefiting them all without selection,
uniting with Heaven and Earth,
this is called virtue."
What is called benevolence?
He said: "Those above do not boast of their accomplishments,
those below do not feel ashamed of their troubles,
do not boast about the great,
do not be dishonest about the small,
Universal love without selfishness,
enduring without decline,
this is what is called rén (仁, benevolence).
What is yì (義, righteousness)?
It is said: Being in a superior position, one should assist the weak;
being in a subordinate position, one should uphold integrity;
when successful, one should not act recklessly;
when impoverished, one should not change one's principles;
acting consistently according to reason;
without selfishly bending the rules,
this is what is called yì (義, righteousness).
What is lǐ (禮, ritual propriety)?
It is said: Being in a superior position, one should be reverent and dignified;
being in a subordinate position, one should be humble and respectful;
yielding and maintaining gentleness,
being the feminine force for the world,
establishing oneself in daring not,
and acting as if incapable;
this is what is called lǐ (禮, ritual propriety).
Therefore, if one cultivates one's Dé (德, virtue), then inferiors will obey orders;
if one cultivates one's rén (仁, benevolence), then inferiors will not contend;
if one cultivates one's yì (義, righteousness), then inferiors will be fair and upright;
if one cultivates one's lǐ (禮, ritual propriety), then inferiors will be respectful;
when these four are cultivated,
the state will be peaceful and secure.
Therefore, that which generates things is the Dào (道, the Way);
that which nurtures them is Dé (德, virtue);
that which loves them is rén (仁, benevolence);
that which rectifies them is yì (義, righteousness);
that which respects them is lǐ (禮, ritual propriety).
Without storing up or nurturing,
things cannot grow and flourish;
without kindness or love,
things cannot be completed and fulfilled.
without rectifying and correcting,
one cannot endure for long;
without reverence and favor,
one cannot be held in high esteem.
Therefore, virtue is what the people value,
benevolence is what the people cherish,
righteousness is what the people fear,
ritual propriety is what the people respect.
These four things
are the alignment of culture,
and what the sage uses to govern all things.
If a ruler lacks virtue, those below will resent him;
if he lacks benevolence, those below will contend with each other;
if he lacks righteousness, those below will be violent;
if he lacks ritual propriety, those below will be in chaos.
If these four principles are not established,
it is called being without the Way.
That one without the Way would not perish,
has never happened.
Lǎozǐ said:
In an age of perfect virtue,
Merchants find convenience in the marketplace,
farmers find joy in the fields,
high officials are content with their positions,
recluses cultivate their Way,
the people rejoice in their occupations.
Therefore, wind and rain do not cause destruction,
grass and trees do not die prematurely,
the Hé River produces a chart,
the Luò River produces a book.
When the age declines,
taxes and levies are without limit,
killing and slaughter are without end,
those who offer criticism are punished,
worthy scholars are killed.
Therefore, mountains collapse and rivers dry up,
even worms and insects cannot rest,
the fields produce no variety of vegetables.
Thus, when the world is well-governed, the foolish cannot cause chaos alone;
when the world is in chaos, the wise cannot govern alone.
Therefore, the sage is harmonious, content, and peaceful.
To be born is [due to]
aspiration attaining the Way and deeds being carried out [is due to]
fate.
Thus, one is born and encounters fate before one can act;
fate encounters the right time before it can be manifest;
there must be the age before there can be the person.
Wén Zǐ asked about sagacity and wisdom.
Lǎo Zǐ said:
To know upon hearing is
sagacity;
to know upon seeing is
wisdom.
Therefore, the sage always hears where misfortune and fortune arise and chooses his path accordingly.
The wise constantly see the formed shapes of misfortune and fortune and choose their actions accordingly.
Sages know the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of the Way of Heaven,
therefore they know the origins of misfortune and fortune.
The wise first see the formed shapes,
therefore they know the gateway to misfortune and fortune.
Knowing before it arises is sagely;
seeing the formed shape first is wise;
those without hearing or seeing
are foolish and deluded.
Lǎozǐ said:
If the ruler is fond of cleverness,
he will act against the times and rely on himself,
abandon calculation and rely on deliberation.
Matters are broad, wisdom is shallow.
To use the shallow to encompass the broad,
there has never been anyone capable of this.
Relying solely on one's wisdom
will surely lead to many mistakes.
Fondness for wisdom
exhausts strategy;
fondness for bravery
is the path to danger and ruin.
If one enjoys giving, then there will be no fixed limits.
If the ruler's limits are not fixed,
then the desires of those below will have no end.
If one levies too much, then one makes enemies of the people.
If one takes little and gives much,
there will be no limit to that number.
Therefore, enjoying giving
is the path to inviting resentment.
From this, if we observe
that wealth is not enough to rely on,
that methods and techniques are what can be relied upon,
it is clear.
Wén Zǐ asked,
"The ancient kings,
how did they govern the world with the Dao?"
How did they do it?
Lǎo Zǐ said,
"Hold fast to the One and do nothing.
Rely on Heaven and Earth to transform things with it.
'The world is a great vessel,
it cannot be grasped,
it cannot be acted upon.

Holding fast to the One

When in a high position,

Being in a high position without overflowing,

If wealth and nobility do not depart from oneself,

Lǎozǐ (老子) said:
The people have a way to follow together,

If the ruler grasps unity, there will be order;
Impermanence means chaos.
The way of the ruler

The wise do not use virtue as a tool for action;

Oneness

the origin of all things.
If a ruler frequently changes the law,

If people use their positions to achieve their likes and dislikes,
the burdens of the subordinates will be so great that they cannot be governed.
Therefore, if the ruler loses oneness,
the chaos will be worse than having no ruler.
The ruler must hold onto oneness before he can unite the masses.
Wén Zǐ asked,

responsive armies,
indignant armies,
greedy armies,

To punish the violent and rescue the weak is called righteousness.

To fight over petty matters and not be able to control one's emotions is called indignation.
To covet the land of others

To rely on the greatness of one's own state,
to boast of the multitude of one's people,

Righteous armies lead to kingship,
responsive armies lead to victory,
indignant armies lead to defeat,
greedy armies lead to death,

Lǎozǐ said:
To abandon the Dào and rely on intelligence is dangerous;
to discard calculation and use talent is to be trapped.
Therefore, adhere to your role and follow principle;
do not worry if you lose,

Accomplishment is not what is deliberately done;
attainment is not what is sought;
entering involves receiving but not taking;
exiting involves giving but not bestowing;
it arises because of spring;
it declines because of autumn;
what is caused to live is not grateful;

Be like the rivers and seas.

Prioritize the small, then the great.
"Those who desire to be above others,

Although in isolated countries and different customs,

Sages are those who

When the era changes, affairs change;

Laws should be established based on the era,
and actions taken in accordance with the time.
The kings of high antiquity
had different laws and measures,

but because the affairs of the time were different.
Therefore, they did not adhere to already established laws,

The laws of the sages are observable,

Their words are worth listening to,
The reason it is said to be beyond form.
The Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors considered the world lightly,
governed all things,
equated death and life,
harmonized with change,
embraced the Dao and promoted sincerity,
using it to reflect the true nature of all things,
associating with the Dao above,
and transforming the people below.
Now, if one wishes to learn their Dao,
but cannot attain its clarity,
while the ruler of the time clings to legal documents,

reduce and hold to the One,

show nothing that is desirable,
'square but not cutting,

Governing them with the Dao will make the people attached,

If you do not show them those who are worthy, the people will be content.
If you do not impose force upon them, the people will be simple.

frugality.
"Do not impose force" means

If you use gifts to gather them,
bribes to take them,
frugality to preserve yourself,

Lǎozǐ said:
What superiors say, inferiors use.

To speak and be certain to be believed,
to promise and be certain to fulfill,

If someone is so upright as to denounce their father,

Therefore, the sage discusses the straight and the crooked in affairs,

There are no constant standards.
To invoke curses is to act like a famed ruler,

the situation makes it so.

is something only the sage can discern.
What starts in conflict and then harmonizes is called "weighing circumstances."
What starts in harmony and then conflicts does not understand "weighing circumstances."
Those who do not understand "weighing circumstances"
can turn good into bad.

To suppress opposition in one's heart;

"To retire when the task is accomplished is the way of Heaven."

The Dao,

from petty cleverness,
Not greatly foolish.

because its mind is focused.

It ends and then begins again,
revolving in the origin of infinity.
Therefore, whether crooked or straight,
what is the use of obtaining it?
Whether straight or crooked,
do not go along with it.

shapes cannot be combined,

The clear water is pure;

Should not be exposed to frost;

Tongue and teeth,

Drawing a bow to shoot;

Things like walking sticks;

Oranges and pomelos have their regions,

Wanting to observe the lands of Jiǔzhōu (九州, ancient China),
