is not preparing for others.
In ancient times, what rulers deeply practiced was called dàodé 道德 (morality and virtue),
In ancient times, those who were rulers,
deep practice was called morality (dào dé);
shallow practice was called benevolence and righteousness (rén yì);
superficial practice was called ritual and wisdom (lǐ zhì).
These six,
are the framework of the state.
Deep practice results in abundant blessings;
shallow practice results in meager blessings;
exhaustively practicing them results in victory over all under Heaven.
In ancient times, cultivating morality (dào dé) meant to rectify all under Heaven;
cultivating benevolence and righteousness (rén yì) meant to rectify one state;
cultivating ritual and wisdom (lǐ zhì) meant to rectify one village.
Those whose virtue is deep are great;
those whose virtue is shallow are small.
Therefore, the Way (dào) is not established by force and might,
is not victorious by firmness and strength,
is not obtained by greed and contention.
Establishment lies in all under Heaven recommending oneself;
victory lies in all under Heaven submitting of their own accord;
attainment lies in all under Heaven giving it,
not in seizing it oneself.
Therefore, the feminine (cí pìn) is established,
the gentle and weak are victorious,
benevolence and righteousness (rén yì) are obtained,
without contention, there is none who can contend with it.
Therefore, the Way (dào) in all under Heaven,
is like the rivers and seas.
The Way of Heaven:
He who acts defeats it;
he who grasps loses it.
Now, if one desires a great reputation and seeks it through struggle,
I see that he has no choice.
Even if he grasps and attains it,
it will not remain.
Reputation cannot be obtained through seeking.
The world bestows it.
Those to whom it is given, it returns.
That to which the world returns
is virtue.
Therefore, it is said:
those of superior dé (德) have the world return to them;
those of superior rén (仁) have all within the seas return to them;
those of superior yì (義) have a state return to them;
those of superior lǐ (禮) have a village return to them.
Lacking these four,
the people will not return.
If they do not return, then one resorts to arms.
Resorting to arms is a dangerous path.
Therefore, it is said:
“Weapons
are inauspicious instruments;
one uses them only when unavoidable.”
Using them causes injury and death.
Winning should not be considered beautiful.
Therefore, it is said:
“Where armies have been
thorns and brambles grow.
One should weep over it with sorrow
and dwell there with funeral rites.”
Therefore, the junzi (君子) strives for morality and virtue,
and does not resort to heavy arms.
Wénzǐ asked, saying:
Why are benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom considered inferior to morality?
Lǎozǐ said:
Those who practice benevolence
must discuss it in terms of sorrow and joy,
those who practice righteousness
must clarify it in terms of taking and giving.
Within the four seas,
sorrow and joy cannot pervade everywhere,
exhausting the wealth and goods of the treasury
is not enough to provide for all the people.
Therefore, it is known that it is better to cultivate the Dao and practice virtue,
follow the nature of Heaven and Earth,
all things will naturally be rectified, and the world will be provided for,
benevolence and righteousness will then be attached [to it].
"Therefore, the great man dwells in what is substantial,
not in what is superficial."
Now, propriety
is the adornment of substance,
benevolence
is the effect of kindness.
Therefore, propriety is established according to human emotions,
However, in reality,
benevolence does not exceed favor,
sorrow is contained within emotion,
and funeral rites are appropriate to benevolence.
When nourishing the living, not forcing people to do what they are unable to,
and not preventing people from doing what they cannot stop themselves from doing,
and keeping measurements within proper limits,
then praise will inevitably arise.
Therefore, the creation of music is sufficient to unite joy,
without exceeding harmony,
clarifying the distinction between life and death,
and understanding the appropriateness of extravagance and frugality.
In degenerate times, it is not like this.
Words contradict actions,
emotions contradict appearances,
rituals are adorned with complexity,
music is disturbed by excess,
customs are corrupted by the world,
and false praise gathers in the court.
Therefore, the perfect man is abandoned and not employed.
If a man races a *jì* (骥) horse on foot,
then the man will not beat the *jì*.
But if he rides in a chariot,
then the *jì* will not beat the man.
Therefore, the one who is good at using the *dào* (道),
relies on the resources of others to establish merit,
using what he is capable of
to support what he is incapable of.
If the ruler gives to the people in due season,
the people will repay him with wealth.
If the ruler treats the people with propriety,
the people will repay him with their lives.
Therefore, there are endangered states but no safe rulers,
and there are worried lords but no happy ministers.
He whose virtue exceeds his position is honored;
he whose salary exceeds his virtue is doomed.
Virtue is valued for being without arrogance;
righteousness is prized for being without excess.
He who is not noble due to virtue
is usurping his position.
He who does not acquire through righteousness
is stealing wealth.
The sage finds peace in poverty and joy in the Dao,
not harming life through desire,
not burdening himself with profit.
Therefore, he does not violate righteousness and take things rashly.
In ancient times, no one was honored without virtue,
no one was made an official without ability,
no one was rewarded without merit,
no one was punished without guilt.
Their advancement of people was done with propriety,
their dismissal of people was done with righteousness.
In the age of petty people,
their advancement of people is as if ascending to heaven,
their dismissal of people is as if casting them into the abyss.
Speaking of the ancients is to criticize the present.
Xiàng Mǎ loses out by focusing on leanness;
selecting officials loses out by focusing on poverty.
Fat pigs fill the kitchen,
but skeletal remains are not given official positions.
A junzi (君子) examines the reality;
do not believe slanderous words.
If a ruler errs and you do not remonstrate,
you are not a loyal minister.
If you remonstrate and are not heeded,
the ruler is unenlightened.
If the people are drowning and you do not worry,
you are not a virtuous ruler.
Therefore, upholding integrity and dying in the face of difficulty
is the duty of a subject.
Clothing against the cold and food against hunger
is the benevolence of a loving father.
Using great things to deal with small things is called transforming a person;
using small things to offend great things is called defying Heaven.
Though one may ascend to heaven in the beginning,
one will inevitably enter the abyss later.
Therefore, in the local village, age is respected,
and the old and impoverished are not neglected.
In the court, rank is based on official titles,
and there are distinctions between the honored and the lowly.
To esteem the noble
means that they are close to the ruler;
to honor the elderly
means that they are close to one's kin;
Respecting elders is like treating them as close older brothers.
Those born into nobility are arrogant,
and those born into wealth are extravagant.
Therefore, if the wealthy and noble do not use understanding of the Dao to examine themselves,
few can avoid doing wrong.
Learning without being satisfied is the way to cultivate oneself.
Teaching without being weary is the way to govern the people.
Having wise teachers and good friends,
few would abandon them and do wrong.
Knowing the worthy is called wisdom;
loving the worthy is called benevolence;
respecting the worthy is called righteousness;
revering the worthy is called propriety;
delighting in the worthy is called joy.
Those who were good at governing the world in ancient times
achieved everything through non-action.
Therefore, governing the world requires tolerance.
If one can achieve this tolerance,
one achieves merit through non-action.
If one cannot achieve this tolerance,
every action will surely lead to misfortune.
To have tolerance in governing the world,
"Be cautious, as if wading through a river in winter;
be circumspect, as if fearing your neighbors;
be dignified, as if a guest;
"Dissolving, it is like melting ice;
Solid, it is like uncarved wood;
Murky, it is like muddy water;
Vast, it is like a valley."
This describes the capacity of the world.
Hesitant, it is like one crossing a river in winter,
not daring to proceed.
Cautious, it is like one fearing the four neighbors,
fearing self-injury.
Solemn, it is like a guest,
carefully practicing respect.
"Dissolving, it is like melting ice,"
not daring to accumulate and store.
"Solid, it is like uncarved wood,"
not daring to cut and shape.
"Murky, it is like muddy water,"
not daring to be clear and bright.
"Vast, it is like a valley,"
not daring to fill and overflow.
"Advancing, not daring to proceed,"
retreating and not daring to be first.
"Fearing self-injury,"
guarding weakness and not daring to boast.
"Careful in respect,"
humbling oneself and respecting others.
"Not daring to accumulate and store,"
diminishing oneself and not daring to be firm.
"Not daring to cut and shape,"
Daring not be whole due to self-perceived deficiency,
daring not be clear and bright
means dwelling in turbidity and disgrace without daring to be fresh,
daring not be overflowing
means seeing inadequacy and daring not to consider oneself worthy.
Indeed, the Dao
retreats, therefore it is able to precede;
it maintains gentleness and weakness, therefore it is able to be strong;
it humbles itself, therefore it is able to surpass others;
it diminishes its flaws, therefore it is truly solid;
it considers itself deficient, therefore it is greatly whole;
it dwells in turbidity and disgrace, therefore it is fresh;
it sees inadequacy, therefore it is able to be worthy.
The Dao acts through non-action, yet there is nothing it does not accomplish.
Superior Meaning
Lǎozǐ said:
"All scholars
should be able to understand the distinction between Heaven and Man,
be versed in the origins of order and chaos,
purify their hearts and clear their minds to preserve it,
and perceive its beginning and end.
Returning to emptiness and nothingness,
may be called reaching the Dao."
The root of governance
is benevolence and righteousness,
its branches
are laws and regulations.
The source of a person's life
is the root;
that which does not give rise to life
is the branch.
Root and branch
are one body.
To love both
is human nature.
To prioritize the root and then the branch
is called a *jūnzǐ* (君子),
to prioritize the branch and then the root
is called a *xiǎorén* (小人).
The origin of laws
is to assist righteousness.
To value law and discard righteousness
is to value one's hat and shoes while forgetting one's head and feet.
Benevolence and righteousness
are expansive and lofty.
To not increase their depth but only expand their breadth leads to ruin.
To not broaden their foundation but only increase their height leads to collapse.
Therefore, if the main beam is not large,
it cannot bear weight.
For bearing weight, nothing is better than the main beam.
For governing a state, nothing is better than virtue.
The ruler's having the people
is like a city's having a foundation,
a tree's having roots.
If the roots are deep, then the base is firm;
If the foundation is solid, then the top will be secure.
Therefore, matters that are not rooted in morality
cannot be considered as classics;
words that do not accord with the former kings
cannot be considered as the Way.
Expedient theories,
and techniques of one action, one accomplishment,
are not the universal path for the world.
Lǎozǐ said:
The way to govern people
is like Zàofù driving a team of four horses.
He harmonizes them with the reins and bit,
and correctly measures them with the chest and breast.
Internally, he grasps the center of their being;
externally, he aligns with the horses' intentions.
Therefore, he can choose the road and reach far,
with energy and strength to spare.
In advancing, retreating, and turning,
nothing is not as he wishes,
truly having mastered the technique.
Now, power and authority
are like the ruler's carriage.
Great ministers
are like the ruler's team of four horses.
The body cannot be separated from the security of the carriage,
and the hand cannot lose the heart of the four horses.
Therefore, if the four horses are not in harmony,
Zào Fù 造父 could not use it to get to the road;
if ruler and minister are not harmonious,
even a sage cannot use it for governing.
Hold to the Dao and use it to manage things,
those of average talent can be fully utilized.
Clearly define roles to show them,
wickedness and deviancy can be stopped.
When things arrive, observe their changes;
when affairs come, respond to their transformations.
If those near are not disordered, then those far away will be governed.
Do not rely on accidental numbers,
but obtain the Dao of nature;
then ten thousand undertakings will not fail.
Lǎozǐ 老子 said:
In general, those who practice the Dao
block devious paths,
guard against what has not yet happened,
do not value being right in themselves,
but value not being able to do wrong.
Therefore, it is said, "Do not make things desirable,
and there will be no day without seeking."
"Do not make things obtainable,"
"and there will be no day without strife."
If this is so, then human desires will be released,
and the public Dao will prevail.
Those who have excess are stopped at the limit,
those who are deficient are helped to meet their needs,
Therefore, the world can be unified.
Now, to abandon duties and listen to praise and blame,
to discard meritorious service and employ cliques,
then unusual skills will lead to flight and concealment,
those who hold office will not advance.
The customs of the people will become disordered in the state,
and meritorious ministers will contend in the court.
Therefore, with the Dao, one governs others,
without the Dao, one is controlled by others.
Lǎozǐ said:
Governing a state has constant principles, but benefiting the people is fundamental.
Political instruction has principles, and making commands and actions proper is paramount.
If it benefits the people,
it is not necessary to follow the ancient ways.
If it is suitable for the matter at hand,
it is not necessary to follow common custom.
Therefore, the sage's laws change with the times,
and rites transform with customs.
Clothing and tools
are each made convenient for their use,
and laws, measures, and decrees
are each adapted to what is appropriate.
Therefore, changing the ancient ways is not necessarily wrong,
and following custom is not necessarily sufficient.
Reciting the books of the former kings
is not as good as hearing their words.
Hearing their words
It is better to grasp the reason behind their words;
to grasp the reason behind their words
is that words cannot fully express it.
Therefore,
"The Dào that can be described
is not the constant Dào.
The name that can be named
is not the constant name."
Therefore, what the sage follows is called Dào,
which is like metal and stone;
once tuned, it cannot be changed.
Affairs are like the qín and sè (zithers);
the tune is changed when the piece ends.
Laws, regulations, rituals, and music
are tools for governing,
not the reason for governing.
Therefore, a narrow-minded scholar cannot be discussed with about the ultimate Dào,
for he is awakened in the mundane and bound by teachings.
Lǎozǐ said:
How can the world have constant laws?
If it fits worldly affairs,
accords with human reason,
is in harmony with Heaven and Earth,
is detailed for ghosts and spirits,
then it can be used for correct governance.
In the past, the Three Sovereigns had no regulations or orders, yet the people followed.
The Five Emperors had regulations and orders but no punishments.
The Xiàhòu Shì (夏后氏) did not break their word.
The Yīn (殷) people made oaths.
The Zhōu (周) people made covenants.
In the decline of the later ages,
people endured disgrace and made light of humiliation,
were greedy for gain and had little shame.
Therefore, laws and decrees
should be discussed among the people, customs should be adjusted to match the urgent needs,
and instruments and weapons
should be adapted to the times and made appropriately suitable.
Those who are bound by the law
cannot undertake distant endeavors.
Those who are constrained by rituals
cannot be made to respond to changes.
One must possess uniquely insightful clarity
and uniquely perceptive hearing
before one can independently chart a course and act.
Those who understand the origins of the law
adapt to the times.
Those who do not know the source of governance
will eventually be thrown into disorder, despite their best efforts.
Now, those who study
follow the precedents of the past,
hold onto written records,
adhere to textual laws,
and wish to govern with them.
This is like holding a square handle and trying to fit it into a round hole.
It is difficult to achieve appropriate suitability.
To preserve the endangered and govern the chaotic,
even the wise are incapable;
advocating antiquity above all,
even the foolish have surplus [wisdom].
Therefore, methods that are not practical,
the sage does not implement;
words that are not verifiable,
the enlightened ruler does not heed.
Wén Zǐ asked,
"Where does law originate?"
Lǎo Zǐ said,
"Law originates from righteousness (yì),
righteousness originates from the suitability to the masses (zhòng shì),
suitability to the masses aligns with the people's hearts;
this is the essence of governance.
Law does not descend from the heavens,
nor does it emerge from the earth;
it arises from among the people,
and turns back to rectify oneself.
If one truly understands its root,
one will not be confused by the branches;
if one knows its essence,
one will not be perplexed by doubts;
if one possesses [a virtue] oneself,
one will not criticize it in others;
if one lacks [a fault] oneself,
one will not demand it of others.
What is established below is not discarded above;
what is prohibited to the people is not practiced by oneself.
Therefore, the ruler's method of establishing laws
is to use them as a standard and model for oneself.
Thus, prohibitions prevail in oneself,
and then orders are carried out among the people.
Now, laws are
the standard of the world
and the measure of the ruler.
To display the laws
is to measure what is lawful and unlawful.
After the laws are established,
those who meet the standard are rewarded,
and those who fall short are punished.
Even the honored and noble are not lightly rewarded,
and even the lowly and base are not severely punished.
Those who violate the law,
even if virtuous, must be punished.
Those who meet the standard,
even if unworthy, are without guilt.
Therefore, impartiality prevails,
and private desires are blocked.
The ancients' establishment of officials
was to restrain the people and prevent them from being self-indulgent.
Their establishment of a ruler
was to control the officials and prevent them from acting independently.
Laws, standards, and methods
are to restrain the ruler and prevent them from acting arbitrarily.
If people are not allowed to be unrestrained,
then the Way will prevail and reason will be attained,
and therefore they will return to inaction.
"Inaction"
does not mean that they do not act at all,
but that they do not proceed from their own desires.
Lǎozǐ said:
"A good rewarder
spends little but encourages much;
a good punisher
uses few punishments but suppresses villainy;
a good giver
uses little resources but creates much virtue;
a good taker
gains much but incurs no resentment."
Therefore, the sage uses what the people like to encourage goodness,
and uses what the people hate to suppress villainy.
If he rewards one person, the whole world will follow him;
if he punishes one person, the whole world will fear him.
Therefore, the highest reward does not cost much,
and the highest punishment is not excessive.
The sage maintains simplicity and governs broadly;
this is what is meant.
Lǎozǐ said:
"The Way of a subject
is to discuss what is appropriate,
To act in advance,
to guard one's position and clarify one's duties,
in order to establish success.
Therefore, when ruler and minister follow different paths, there is order;
when they follow the same path, there is chaos.
Each obtains what is appropriate,
occupies the position that is fitting,
thus superiors and inferiors have means to employ each other.
Therefore, branches must not be larger than the trunk,
the end must not be stronger than the root;
it speaks to how weight, importance, size can mutually restrain each other.
Now, those who obtain power and influence,
what they hold is very little,
what they entrust is very great,
what they guard is very compact,
what they control is very extensive;
a tree ten spans in circumference,
supports a house weighing a thousand *jūn*,
this is what obtaining power brings.
A gate five inches in size,
can control opening and closing,
what it occupies is crucial.
Commands that must be carried out below,
those who comply will benefit,
those who oppose will suffer harm,
that the world all listens and obeys,
is compliance.
To issue commands and enforce prohibitions,
Relying on the multitude is [how to build] power.
Righteousness,
is not necessarily about being able to fully benefit all the people under Heaven.
[Rather, it's about] benefiting one person, and the whole world will follow.
Tyranny,
is not necessarily about being able to fully harm everyone within the seas.
[Rather, it's about] harming one person, and the whole world will rebel.
Therefore, every action taken, and every discarding,
must be carefully considered.
Lǎozǐ 老子 said:
"To bend an inch to stretch a foot,
to slightly wrong to greatly straighten,
this is what a sage does."
Nowadays, when rulers assess their ministers,
they do not consider their great accomplishments.
They scrutinize their minor actions
and seek out their small virtues,
which is the way to lose talented men.
Therefore, if a person has profound virtue,
do not question their minor details.
If a person has great renown,
do not find fault with their small mistakes.
Human nature is such that everyone has shortcomings.
Completing their grand strategy is what matters;
even if they have small faults,
it is not enough to hold them back.
If they fail to complete their grand strategy,
To behave in the manner of a common villager
is not sufficient.
Therefore, those who are overly cautious achieve no success,
those with flawed conduct are not tolerated by the masses,
those who are of great stature are lax in details,
those with a grand vision have far-reaching reputations;
this is the way to evaluate ministers.
Lǎozǐ said:
From ancient times until now,
there has never been anyone who could be perfect in their conduct.
Therefore, a noble person does not demand perfection from one individual,
being "square but not cutting,
honest but not injuring,
straight but not unrestrained,"
broad-minded and not fault-finding.
Morality and martial prowess
should not be demanded with perfection from human capability,
self-cultivation through the Dao,
rather than demanding it from others,
is easily compensated.
Self-cultivation through the Dao
will then be without fault.
Indeed, the jade ring of the Xià Hòu clan
cannot be without flaws,
the pearl of the bright moon
cannot be without blemish,
yet the world treasures them,
Do not let small evils obscure great beauty.
Now, focusing on people's shortcomings,
and forgetting their strengths,
while desiring to seek out the worthy in the world,
is truly difficult.
The views of the masses,
those of low position and humble status,
and those concerned with degrading matters,
do not understand the greater picture.
Therefore, the way to judge people
is to observe what people they recommend when they are honored,
observe how they give when they are wealthy,
observe what they will not accept when they are poor,
observe what they will not do when they are lowly,
observe the difficulties they find themselves in,
in order to know their courage.
Observe their steadfastness when they are moved by joy and happiness.
in order to see how they guard themselves.
Entrust them with money and goods,
in order to observe their benevolence.
Shake them with fear and trepidation,
in order to observe their integrity.
If you do this,
then human nature can be understood.
Lǎozǐ said:
To yield is how one seeks to extend;
to bend is how one seeks to straighten.
To bend an inch to extend a foot,
to take a small wrong to achieve a great right,
the noble person does this.
A hundred rivers flow side by side;
those that do not flow into the sea cannot be called valleys.
One rushes to different places;
those who do not return to goodness cannot be called noble persons (jūnzǐ).
Good words are valued for their feasibility,
good deeds are valued for their benevolence and righteousness.
Indeed, the faults of a noble person (jūnzǐ)
are like the eclipses of the sun and moon;
they do not obscure their brightness.
Therefore, the wise do not act rashly,
the brave do not kill indiscriminately;
they choose what is right and do it,
they consider propriety and act accordingly.
Thus, when affairs are accomplished, their merits are reliable;
when their bodies die, their names are worthy of praise.
Even if one has intelligence and ability,
one must establish it upon benevolence and righteousness as the foundation,
Intelligence and ability act together;
sages take benevolence and righteousness as the standard.
Those who meet the standard are called noble persons (jūnzǐ),
those who do not meet the standard are called petty persons (xiǎorén).
Although the noble person (jūnzǐ) dies,
his name does not perish.
Although the petty person (xiǎorén) gains power,
his sins are not pardoned.
To hold the map of the world in the left hand,
and to cut one's own throat with the right hand,
even a fool would not do that;
one's life is more precious than the world.
Those who die in the difficulty of their lord and parents,
see death as returning home.
殘賊天下，
the myriad people are in turmoil,
with no place to find peace.
A sage suddenly rises up,
to punish the violent and oppressive,
to pacify the chaotic world,
to eliminate harm for the world,
to turn the muddy into the clear,
to turn danger into peace,
therefore, he cannot but intervene.
Chìdì (赤帝) caused fire disasters,
therefore Huángdì (黃帝) captured him.
Gònggōng (共工) caused water damage,
therefore Zhuānxū (顓頊) executed him.
If you teach them with the Dao,
guide them with virtue but they do not listen,
then you confront them with might and force.
If even then they do not comply,
then you subdue them with weapons and armor.
Killing innocent people,
supporting an unrighteous ruler,
there is no greater harm;
exhausting the wealth of the world,
to satisfy the desires of one person,
there is no deeper disaster;
indulging the desires of one person,
and prolonging the suffering within the realm,
this is what Heaven's natural order does not allow.
The reason for establishing a ruler
is to prevent violence and chaos.
Now, relying on the strength of the people,
he instead becomes cruel and tyrannical.
This is like giving wings to a tiger;
why would he not be removed?
Those who raise fish
must eliminate the *piāntà* (otters and similar predators).
Those who raise birds and beasts
must eliminate the jackals and wolves,
how much more so when governing the people!
This is why weapons of war arise.
Lǎozǐ said:
"The way to govern a state
is to have no harsh commands from above,
no troublesome administration from officials,
no false conduct from scholars,
no extravagant craftsmanship from artisans.
Affairs are entrusted without disturbance,
and tools are complete without embellishment.
In a chaotic world, it is not like this.
Those who act compete in exalting themselves,
those who practice propriety compete in pretension.
Carriages are excessively carved and polished,
utensils are excessively engraved.
Those seeking wealth contend for what is difficult to obtain and deem it precious.
Those criticizing writing pursue complexity and consider it urgent.
Matters conducted with false arguments,
prolonged and unresolved,
are of no benefit to governance,
but beneficial to chaos.
Crafting elaborate and intricate tools,
which take years to complete,
are not practical in application.
Now, the method of Shénnóng 神農 states:
if a man, being strong and able-bodied, does not plow,
then the world will have those who suffer hunger;
if a woman, in her prime, does not weave,
then the world will have those who suffer cold.
Therefore, he himself personally plowed,
and his wife personally wove,
setting an example for the world.
His guiding of the people
was "not valuing goods that are hard to obtain,"
and not treasuring useless things.
Therefore, if the plower does not exert himself,
he will have nothing with which to nourish his life;
if the weaver does not exert her strength,
she will have nothing with which to clothe her form.
If there is surplus or deficiency,
each is responsible for their own situation.
With clothing and food abundant and plentiful,
wickedness and evil do not arise,
peace and happiness prevail without incident,
the world is at peace.
The wise have no place to apply their strategies,
the brave have no place to display their might.
Lǎozǐ said:
The way of the hegemon
is to deliberate with schemes,
to plan with strategies,
to act upholding righteousness.
It is not for the sake of survival,
but for the sake of survival and extinction.
Therefore, upon hearing that the ruler of an enemy state
is tyrannical towards his people,
immediately raise troops and approach its borders,
accuse him of unrighteousness,
and denounce his excessive actions.
When the army reaches its outskirts,
instruct the military commander, saying:
"Do not cut down trees,
do not dig up graves,
do not ruin the five grains,
do not burn accumulated stores,
do not capture the people as prisoners,
do not gather the six domestic animals";
then issue orders and decrees, saying:
"The ruler of that state
goes against Heaven and Earth,
insults ghosts and spirits,
renders unjust verdicts,
Killing the innocent is not without consequences.
It is what Heaven condemns,
and what the people detest.
The coming of armies
is to abolish injustice and receive their virtue.
Those who dare to defy the Way of Heaven
and are treacherous to the people
will suffer death and the extermination of their clan.
Those families who listen to us will be rewarded by families,
those neighborhoods who listen will be rewarded by neighborhoods,
those districts who listen will be enfeoffed as lords of districts.
Conquer their state but do not harm their people,
depose their ruler,
change their government,
honor their outstanding scholars,
promote their virtuous and capable,
provide for their orphans and widows,
care for their poor,
release those imprisoned,
reward those who have contributed.
The people will open their doors to welcome them,
soak rice to store for them,
only worried that they will not come.
When a righteous army arrives at the border,
the fighting will cease without a battle.
An unrighteous army,
on the other hand, will arrive amidst corpses and flowing blood,
crossing over each other in the advance.
Therefore, those who fight for territory
cannot establish their kingship.
Those who seek for themselves
cannot establish their merit.
Those who undertake affairs for the sake of others
will be assisted by the masses.
Those who act for their own benefit
will be abandoned by the masses.
Those who are assisted by the masses,
though weak, will surely become strong.
Those who are abandoned by the masses,
though great, will surely perish.
Lǎozǐ 老子 said:
The highest form of righteousness
is to govern the state,
manage the territory,
practice benevolence and righteousness,
spread virtue and bestow favors,
establish correct laws,
block perverse paths,
making ministers close and attached,
and the people harmonious and united.
With the superiors and inferiors of one mind,
and all the ministers united in strength,
the feudal lords will submit to his majesty,
and the four directions will cherish his virtue.
He cultivates governance in the temple court,
To parry attacks a thousand *lǐ* away,
to issue orders and commands to which the world responds –
this is the highest level.
To have a vast territory and a large population,
a wise ruler and capable generals,
a wealthy state and strong soldiers,
reliable commitments,
and clear orders;
when two enemies are evenly matched,
before they engage in battle with weapons drawn,
the enemy flees –
this is the next level.
To know the suitability of the land,
to be familiar with the advantages of strategic passes,
to understand the changes between surprise attacks and conventional warfare,
to examine the matters of troop formations;
when blades clash,
and arrows fly,
carts carry the dead and support the wounded,
blood flows for a thousand *lǐ*,
and exposed corpses fill the fields –
this is the lowest level of righteousness.
The victory or defeat of an army all lies in governance.
If the governance wins over its people,
and the people are attached to their superiors,
then the army is strong.
If the people overcome their governance,
and the people rebel against their superiors,
and thus the army is weak.
Therefore, virtue and righteousness are sufficient to win the hearts of the people of the world,
achievements are sufficient to meet the urgent needs of the world,
selection and appointment are sufficient to gain the hearts of worthy scholars,
plans and considerations are sufficient to decide the weight of power;
this is the way of supreme righteousness.
Lǎozǐ said:
That which makes a state strong must face death,
and that which faces death must be righteousness.
That which allows righteousness to be carried out is authority.
Therefore, command with civility,
and regulate with martial force;
this is called certain victory.
When authority and righteousness go hand in hand,
this is called certain strength.
When swords clash and meet,
and arrows and stones fall like rain,
and the soldiers compete to be first,
it is because rewards are trustworthy and punishments are clear.
If the superior regards the inferior as a child,
the inferior will serve the superior as a father;
if the superior regards the inferior as a younger brother,
the inferior will serve the superior as an elder brother;
if the superior regards the inferior as a child,
he will surely reign over the four seas;
if the inferior regards the superior as a father,
he will surely rectify the world;
When superiors regard subordinates as younger brothers,
then it is not difficult for them to die for them.
When subordinates serve superiors as elder brothers,
then it is not difficult for them to flee for them.
Therefore, one should not fight with enemies among fathers, sons, and brothers.
Therefore, a righteous ruler cultivates his government internally
to accumulate virtue,
externally blocking evil
to clarify his power,
observing their toil and ease
to understand their hunger and satiety.
When the date of battle is set,
and death is regarded as returning home,
it is the increase of kindness.
*Shàng Lǐ* (Above Rituals):
Lǎozǐ said:
In ancient times, the True People
breathed in the yin and yang,
and all living beings invariably relied on their virtue for harmony and obedience.
At that time,
everyone was in order,
things were formed in secrecy and naturally,
purity and simplicity were not scattered,
and all things were greatly abundant.
When the world declined,
to the time of Fúxī Shì,
mèi mèi mào mào,
All wanted to depart from their childlike minds,
And awaken to the space between Heaven and Earth,
Their virtue became troubled and inconsistent.
Coming to Shénnóng
and Huángdì,
They examined and governed the world,
Ordered and controlled the four seasons,
Harmonized and adjusted Yin and Yang,
Whereupon the myriad people all stood upright and pondered,
Raised their heads to listen and looked intently,
Therefore, they governed but could not harmonize.
Down to the eras of the Xià
and Yīn dynasties,
Desires were connected to things,
Intelligence was enticed by externals,
And the true nature of life was lost.
Extending to the Zhōu dynasty,
Pureness was diminished and simplicity scattered,
Deviating from the Way to embrace falsehood,
Considering dangerous virtue as proper conduct,
Cunning ingenuity sprouted,
Imitating sages through cunning learning,
Using extravagant rhetoric to coerce the masses,
Polishing and embellishing poetry and books,
To trade for fame and reputation,
Each wanted to implement their clever falsehoods,
To be accepted by the world,
And lost the foundation of the great ancestor.
Therefore, the world experienced the loss of life,
The decline and gradual descent have been a long time coming.
Therefore, the learning of the supreme person,
is to return the nature to nothingness [wú],
And roam the mind in emptiness;
The learning of the common people [shì sú],
displays virtue and plucks at nature,
causing internal worry in the five viscera,
and violent actions that exceed knowledge,
in order to clamor for fame and reputation in the world.
This is what the perfected person [zhì rén] does not do.
To display virtue is to seek self-manifestation;
to pluck at nature is to cut off life.
As for the perfected person [zhì rén], they are settled within the realm of life and death,
understand the principle of honor and disgrace.
If the whole world praises them, they are not further encouraged;
if the whole world criticizes them, they are not further discouraged.
This is because they have grasped the essence of the supreme Dao.
Lǎozǐ said:
"In ancient times, people wore their hair loose and without collars
to rule the world.
Their virtue was to give life and not to kill,
to bestow and not to take away.
The world did not criticize their clothing
and embraced their virtue together.
At that time,
the Yin and Yang were in harmony,
and all things flourished.
The nests of flying birds
could be reached down and taken,
and running beasts could be tied up and led."
When it declined,
birds, beasts, insects, and snakes
all become harmful to people.
Therefore, iron is cast and blades are forged
to defend against their danger.
When the people are pressed by difficulties, they seek convenience;
because of their troubles, they create preparations.
Each uses their wisdom
to eliminate what harms them
and embrace what benefits them.
Old customs cannot be followed perpetually,
and tools cannot be relied upon indefinitely.
Therefore, the laws and measures of the former kings
were subject to change.
Thus it is said:
"The name that can be named
is not the constant name."
The Five Emperors (Wǔ Dì) differed in their methods but their virtue covered the world.
The Three Kings (Sān Wáng) had different affairs, but their names were established for later generations.
This is because they changed with the times.
It is like Shī Kuàng's 調 (tiáo) tuning of the five tones;
the adjustments he makes up and down are not constant,
yet the dimensions are measured
And none will miss the mark.
Therefore, those who understand the essence of music can create it.
Words must have a fundamental basis within.
And those who know how to use compasses, squares, hooks, and lines can govern people.
Therefore, the institutions of the former kings
should not be hastily discarded,
and the affairs of later generations
should be recorded if they are good.
Therefore, the sage who establishes rituals and music
is not constrained by rituals and music.
The one who controls things
is not controlled by things.
The one who establishes laws
is not constrained by laws.
Therefore, it is said:
“The Dao that can be spoken of
is not the constant Dao.”
Lǎozǐ said:
In the past, the sage kings
looked up to take their patterns from Heaven,
looked down to take their measures from Earth,
and took their models from humanity in the middle.
They harmonized the qi of yin and yang,
and harmonized the seasons of the four times.
They observed the suitability of hills, lands, waters, marshes, fertile and barren soils, high and low grounds,
to establish affairs and generate wealth,
to eliminate the suffering of hunger and cold,
To ward off the disasters of pestilence and disease,
[One] received human affairs,
and thereby established rites and music,
practiced the way of benevolence and righteousness,
and thereby governed human relationships.
[One] arranged the natures of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth,
and thereby established the affection between father and son, completing the family;
[One] listened to the numbers produced by the clear and turbid tones of the five notes and the generation of the six lǜ (pitch pipes),
and thereby established the righteousness between ruler and minister, completing the state;
[One] observed the order of the first, middle, and last months of the four seasons,
and thereby established the decorum between elder and younger, completing the officialdom;
[One] divided the land into zhōu (provinces),
assigned offices and governed them,
and established great schools to teach them;
these are the guiding principles of governance.
If one attains the Dao, then [one is] promoted;
if one loses the Dao, then [one is] dismissed.
Now, there has never been a thing that stretches without relaxing,
or that succeeds without failing;
only the sage can succeed without declining.
When the sage first created music,
it was to return to the spirits and block licentiousness,
restoring [people's] heavenly nature;
when it declined,
it flowed away and did not return,
[people] became licentious and fond of sensual pleasures,
even to the point of destroying the state.
When [the sage] first created writing,
In governing and managing all affairs,
the foolish rely on not forgetting,
while the wise rely on recording events.
When it declines,
they resort to deceit and falsehood to exonerate the guilty,
and to kill the innocent.
In creating parks and gardens,
they do so to supply the implements for ancestral temples,
and to train soldiers to prepare for unforeseen events.
When it declines,
they race around hunting and shooting, seizing the people's time,
and exhausting the people's strength.
In valuing the worthy,
they do so to harmonize teachings and customs,
and to rectify legal disputes.
When the worthy are in positions,
and the capable are in offices,
blessings are bestowed upon those below,
and the myriad people cherish virtue.
When it declines,
cliques and factions form alliances,
each promoting their own associates,
abandoning the public for private interests,
with internal and external forces colluding.
The treacherous are in positions,
and the worthy live in seclusion.
The way of Heaven and Earth
Extremes revert.
Excesses diminish.
Therefore, the sage rulers govern what is corrupt and change the system.
When matters are concluded, they change again.
Their beauty lies in harmony.
Their fault lies in the abuse of power.
The way of the sage rulers says:
If one does not cultivate ritual propriety (lǐyì),
Integrity and shame (liánchǐ) will not be established.
If the people have no integrity and shame,
They cannot be governed.
If they do not know ritual propriety,
Law cannot rectify them.
If one does not exalt good and abolish ugliness,
People will not be inclined toward ritual propriety.
Without law, there is nothing that cannot be used for governing;
If one does not know ritual propriety,
One cannot implement law.
Law can kill those who are unfilial,
But it cannot make people filial.
It can punish thieves,
But it cannot make people honest.
When the sage kings are on top,
They make clear what is liked and disliked to show the people.
They guide them with constant praise and blame.
They are close to the worthy and advance them.
They despise the unworthy and remove them.
Punishments are set aside and not used.
By cultivating propriety and righteousness, they are entrusted with the virtuous and capable.
Therefore, the highest in the world
are made the Sāngōng (三公, Three Dukes),
the highest in a province
are made the Jiǔqīng (九卿, Nine Ministers),
the highest in a state
are made the twenty-seven Dàfū (大夫, Grand Masters),
and the highest in a village
are made the eighty-one Yuánshì (元士, Primary Scholars).
Those whose wisdom surpasses ten thousand people are called Yīng (英, Outstanding),
those whose wisdom surpasses a thousand people are called Jùn (雋, Eminent),
those whose wisdom surpasses a hundred people are called Jié (傑, Exceptional),
and those whose wisdom surpasses ten people are called Háo (豪, Prominent).
One who is enlightened about the Way of Heaven and Earth,
understands the principles of human affairs,
is magnanimous enough to accommodate the masses,
is benevolent enough to cherish those far away,
and is wise enough to understand expediency,
is an Yīng (英).
One whose virtue is sufficient to teach and transform,
whose conduct is sufficient to embody righteousness,
whose trustworthiness is sufficient to gain the support of the masses,
and whose clarity is sufficient to illuminate those below,
is a Jùn (雋).
One whose conduct can serve as a model,
whose wisdom is sufficient to resolve doubts,
whose trustworthiness allows them to keep their word,
whose integrity allows them to distribute wealth fairly,
Acting can be modeled,
speaking can be followed,
this is a outstanding person (rén jié) .
Upholding one's duty without neglect,
abiding by righteousness without partiality,
facing difficulty without seeking easy escape,
seeing profit without seeking improper gain,
this is a hero (rén háo).
The elite and outstanding heroes (yīng jùn háo jié),
each according to the size of their talent are placed in their respective positions,
from the root flowing to the branches,
using the heavy to control the light,
the superiors initiate and the subordinates respond in harmony,
within the four seas,
with one heart, all return to the same [goal],
turning their backs on greed and meanness,
and turning towards benevolence and righteousness,
in transforming the people,
it is like the wind bending the grass.
Now, if the unworthy are placed above the worthy,
even strict punishments cannot prevent their wickedness,
the small cannot control the large,
the weak cannot command the strong,
this is the nature of Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, the sage elevates the worthy to establish merit,
while an unworthy ruler elevates those with whom he is in agreement.
Observe whom they elevate,
and order and disorder are distinguished;
By observing their associates,
one can discuss whether they are virtuous or not.
Lǎozǐ 老子 said:
"Those who practice ritual
carve and chisel human nature,
correcting and brushing aside its feelings.
Though the eyes desire something, they are restrained by measure;
though the heart delights in something, it is regulated by ritual.
Running and circling,
bowing and prostrating in humility,
meat congeals but is not eaten,
wine is clarified but not drunk.
Outwardly, their form is constrained;
inwardly, their will is troubled.
They clamp down on the harmony of Yīn 陰 and Yáng 陽 and oppress the feelings of nature and life.
Therefore, they are mourners for life.
Why?
Because they do not address the reason for their desires
but forbid what is desired;
they do not understand the reason for their joy
but guard against what is joyful.
This is like building a pen for animals without reinforcing the walls,
but forbidding their wild instincts;
or diverting the flow of a river but trying to dam it with one's hand.
Therefore, it is said:
'Open its passages,
assist its affairs,
zhōngshēn bù jiù." (will not be saved in the end.)
Fú lǐ zhě, (Now, rites,)
è qíng bì yù, (restrain emotions and shut off desires,)
yǐ yì zì fáng, (using righteousness to guard oneself,)
suī qíng xīn yē yè, (even if emotions in the heart sob,)
xíng xìng jī kě, (and the physical nature is hungry and thirsty,)
yǐ bùdéyǐ zì qiáng, (one forces oneself with "cannot be helped",)
gù mò néng zhōng qí tiānnián. (therefore, no one can complete their natural lifespan.)
Lǐ zhě, (Rites,)
fēi néng shǐ rén wù yù yě, (cannot make people not desire,)
ér néng zhǐ zhī, (but can stop them,)
yuè zhě, (music,)
fēi néng shǐ rén wù lè yě, (cannot make people not enjoy,)
ér néng fáng zhī. (but can prevent them.)
Fú shǐ tiānxià tóng wèi xíng ér bù gǎn dàoqiè, (Now, making the world equally fear punishment and not dare to steal,)
qǐ ruò shǐ wú yǒu dào xīn zāi! (is it as good as making them have no heart for stealing?)
Gù zhī qí wú suǒ yòng, (Therefore, if one knows that something is useless,)
suī tān zhě jiē cí zhī, (even the greedy will refuse it,)
bùzhī qí wú suǒ yòng, (if one does not know that something is useless,)
lián zhě bùnéng ràng zhī. (even the incorruptible cannot yield it.)
Fú rén zhī suǒyǐ wáng shèjì, (Now, the reason people lose their state,)
shēn sǐ rén shǒu, (die by others' hands,)
wèi tiānxià xiào zhě, (and are laughed at by the world,)
wèicháng fēi yù yě, (has never not been because of desires,)
zhī dōng rì zhī shàn, (knowing that a fan in winter,)
xià rì zhī qiú, (or a fur coat in summer,)
wú yòng yú jǐ, (is useless to oneself,)
zé wànwù biàn wèi chén gòu yǐ! (then all things become like dust and dirt!)
Therefore, if you scoop out boiling water to stop the boiling,
the boiling will only become even worse.
Those who understand the root cause
simply remove the fire.
Lǎozǐ said:
"To follow one's nature and act accordingly is called the Dao;
to attain one's natural disposition is called Virtue.
Only when nature is lost do we value benevolence;
only when the Dao is lost do we value righteousness.
When benevolence and righteousness are established, morality and virtue are discarded;
when pure simplicity is scattered, then rituals and music adorn things;
when right and wrong take shape, then the common people are bewildered;
when pearls and jade are prized, then the world contends."
Now, rituals
are that by which one distinguishes noble and base, honored and lowly;
righteousness
is that by which one harmonizes the relationships between ruler and subject, father and son, brothers, husband and wife, the interactions of humanity.
The rituals of the degenerate age
are reverent, yet transactional.
Those who act righteously
bestow gifts in order to gain;
ruler and subject criticize each other,
and family members breed resentment.
Therefore, when water accumulates, it breeds mutually devouring insects;
when soil accumulates, it breeds beasts that feed on their own flesh;
when rituals and music adorn things, it breeds deceit and falsehood.
The governance of a degenerate age
Not accumulating the means of nourishing life,
diluting the purity of the world,
scattering the simplicity of the world,
confusing the people,
taking clarity as turbidity,
with life and destiny scattered,
all thrown into chaos by scheming,
integrity and trustworthiness decayed and ruined,
people lose their nature,
law and righteousness oppose each other,
conduct and profit contradict each other,
the poor and rich antagonize each other,
the lord and the servant are not different,
not worth discussing.
For if there is abundance, then yield;
if there is deficiency, then contend.
Yielding gives rise to ritual and righteousness;
contention gives rise to violence and disorder.
Therefore, with many desires, affairs are not examined;
seeking abundance, contention does not cease.
Therefore, when the world is well-governed, petty people uphold righteousness,
and profit cannot entice them.
When the world is chaotic, gentlemen engage in treachery,
and the law cannot restrain them.
Lǎozǐ said:
The ruler of a declining age
drills into mountains for rocks,
To seize gold and jade,
To extract máonɡ and shèn shells,
To melt down copper and iron,
And myriad things will not flourish;
To disembowel the womb and burn the suburbs,
To overturn nests and destroy eggs,
The fènghuáng bird will not soar,
The qílín will not roam,
To construct wooden platforms,
To burn forests for hunting,
To drain ponds for fishing,
To pile up earth and dwell on mounds,
To dig the earth and drink from wells,
To dredge rivers and make ponds,
To build cities for fortification,
To confine beasts for livestock;
Then the yīnyáng will be confused and contradictory,
The four seasons will lose their order,
Thunder and lightning will be destructive,
Hail and frost will cause harm,
Myriad things will be scorched and withered,
Dying in great numbers,
Grasses and trees will wither in summer,
The three rivers will be cut off and cease to flow.
To divide mountains, rivers, streams, and valleys,
Establishing territorial boundaries,
To calculate the multitude and scarcity of people,
Establishing numerical divisions,
If one sets up mechanical barriers as defenses,
establishes official colors,
differentiates ranks to distinguish the noble from the base,
makes distinctions between the worthy and the unworthy,
and enacts rewards and punishments,
then warfare will arise, and resentment and contention will be produced,
innocent people will be cruelly murdered,
and punishments will be inflicted on the guiltless.
This is where it begins.
Lǎozǐ said:
When the world is about to lose its nature and its lives,
it is like the rising of dark energy.
The ruler is benighted and does not understand,
the Dao is abandoned and not practiced,
virtue is extinguished and not promoted,
actions are contrary to Heaven,
edicts are issued in opposition to the four seasons,
the spring and autumn cycles lose their harmony,
Heaven and Earth eliminate their virtue.
The ruler is in his position but not at ease,
high officials go into hiding and do not speak,
the assembled ministers conform to the ruler's will and harbor their own agendas,
they distance themselves from their own flesh and blood to protect themselves,
crooked people flatter and scheme in secret,
hastily supporting the arrogant ruler and mimicking his intentions,
causing chaos to achieve their own ends.
Therefore, the assembled ministers are at odds and not intimate,
Kinsmen are estranged and do not cleave together;
In the fields, no seedlings stand;
On the roads, no one walks leisurely;
Accumulated gold is sold at a discount;
Doubled jade offerings yield no profit;
Tortoise shells are without underbellies;
Divination with yarrow stalks is practiced daily;
The world is not united as one family;
The feudal lords establish laws and customs that differ from each other.
They violently uproot and discard the foundation;
They carve out the Five Punishments;
They engage in engraving and whittling;
They contend over the tips of awls and knives;
They cut down the common people;
Slaying more than half of them;
Raising troops causes hardship;
Attacking cities results in indiscriminate slaughter;
Toppling what is high endangers what is secure;
With large siege engines,
High and heavy earthworks,
Except war battles,
Causing battle death on the way,
Opposing strong enemy,
The people rebel at the first opportunity;
Reputation is sought superficially;
Annexing countries to gain territory,
Corpses pile up by the hundreds of thousands;
The old and weak die of hunger and cold,
Their number is uncountable.
From this point on,
The world has never been able to secure its life,
Or enjoy its customs.
Sages and worthies suddenly rise up,
Holding fast to morality and virtue.
assisting with benevolence and righteousness,
those nearby were promoted for their wisdom,
those far away cherished their virtue,
the world was unified,
descendants succeeded one another,
and assistants were capable.
They rejected the instigation of slanderers,
stopped the talk of petty sophistry,
eliminated harsh and oppressive laws,
removed troublesome and excessive affairs,
suppressed traces of gossip and rumors,
blocked the gates of factions and cliques,
extinguished cleverness,
followed the great constant,
abandoned limbs and appendages (i.e., outward adornments),
rejected intelligence and wisdom,
achieved great harmony and oneness,
and all things returned to their roots.
The sage is not able to bring about the right time,
but when the time arrives, he does not fail to seize it,
and thus he cannot be cut off halfway.
Lǎozǐ said:
"The depth of the Fēng River is ten *rèn*, yet it does not accept dust and dirt;
though gold and iron are within it,
their shapes are visible from the outside.
It is not that it is not deep and clear,
yet fish, turtles, and dragons do not return to it."
Five grains do not grow on stone,
bald mountains are not roamed by mì deer,
because there is nothing to shade or shelter them.
Therefore, if governing is taking severity as discernment,
taking strictness as clarity,
taking harshness to subordinates as loyalty,
taking many calculations as merit,
those who do so,
are like stretching leather;
it may be large,
but it is the way to tear it.
'When the government is patient,
the people are simple.
When the government is intrusive,
the people are cunning.'”
Lǎozǐ said:
"Govern the state with uprightness,
use surprise in war."
First, establish a government that cannot be overcome,
and then seek to overcome the enemy.
Using what is untamed to attack the disorder of others
This is like using fire to respond to fire,
or using water to respond to water.
Things that are the same are not sufficient to govern each other,
therefore difference is valued as extraordinary.
Tranquility is extraordinary to agitation,
order is extraordinary to chaos,
satiation is extraordinary to hunger,
ease is extraordinary to toil.
The correspondence of the extraordinary and the normal
is like the succession of water, fire, metal, and wood.
Where can one go and not be victorious?
Therefore, if virtue is equal, then the many will defeat the few;
if strength is matched, then the wise will control the foolish;
if wisdom is the same, then those with a plan will capture the unplanned.
